// Horizontal layered (BFS) layout for heap objects.
//
// The heap is a directed graph: objects (structs/arrays) with pointer fields
// that reference other objects. We lay it out left-to-right:
//   - depth (distance from a root) -> column (x), increasing rightward
//   - siblings within a depth       -> stacked vertically (y)
// Roots are heap objects pointed to by stack variables; unreachable objects
// (e.g. leaked mallocs) are laid out as their own trees after the reachable
// ones so nothing is hidden.
//
// This renders trees as trees (root left, children fanning right), linked
// lists as left-to-right chains, and cycles/graphs honestly: a back-edge is
// just an arrow returning to an earlier node. It never duplicates or drops a
// node — a shared child is placed once and both parents point at it.

import {
  type ProgramState,
  type HeapObject,
  isArray,
  isStruct,
  isRef,
} from "./trace";

export interface NodeLayout {
  id: string;
  /** Top-left position within the layout canvas, in px. */
  x: number;
  y: number;
  depth: number;
}

export interface HeapLayout {
  nodes: Map<string, NodeLayout>;
  /** Total canvas size needed to fit every node. */
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

// Spacing between columns (depth) and rows (siblings). These are generous so
// boxes of varying size don't collide; the stage scrolls if it overflows.
const COL_GAP = 190; // horizontal distance between depth levels
const ROW_GAP = 130; // vertical distance between stacked nodes
const PAD = 16;

/** The heap-object ids a given object points at, in field/cell order. */
function childIdsOf(obj: HeapObject): string[] {
  const ids: string[] = [];
  if (isArray(obj)) {
    for (const el of obj.elements) {
      if (isRef(el) && el.target && el.target.kind === "heap") {
        ids.push(el.target.id);
      }
    }
  } else if (isStruct(obj)) {
    for (const f of obj.fields) {
      if (isRef(f.value) && f.value.target && f.value.target.kind === "heap") {
        ids.push(f.value.target.id);
      }
    }
  }
  return ids;
}

/** Heap objects referenced directly by a stack variable (the layout roots). */
function rootIds(state: ProgramState): string[] {
  const roots: string[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const frame of state.stack) {
    for (const v of frame.variables) {
      if (isRef(v.value) && v.value.target && v.value.target.kind === "heap") {
        const id = v.value.target.id;
        if (!seen.has(id)) {
          seen.add(id);
          roots.push(id);
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return roots;
}

/**
 * Compute positions for every heap object via BFS from the roots. Each node's
 * depth is its shortest distance from a root; nodes are packed into vertical
 * "slots" per depth so siblings don't overlap. Returns absolute positions and
 * the canvas size.
 */
export function layoutHeap(state: ProgramState): HeapLayout {
  const heap = state.heap;
  const allIds = Object.keys(heap);
  const nodes = new Map<string, NodeLayout>();

  // Assign a depth to every reachable node via BFS. Start from stack roots;
  // then seed any still-unvisited objects (unreachable/leaked) as new roots so
  // they still appear.
  const depth = new Map<string, number>();
  const queue: string[] = [];

  const enqueueRoot = (id: string) => {
    if (!depth.has(id) && heap[id]) {
      depth.set(id, 0);
      queue.push(id);
    }
  };

  rootIds(state).forEach(enqueueRoot);
  // Seed unreachable objects as additional roots (stable order).
  for (const id of allIds) enqueueRoot(id);

  // BFS, recording the order nodes are first reached at each depth.
  const byDepth = new Map<number, string[]>();
  let head = 0;
  while (head < queue.length) {
    const id = queue[head++];
    const d = depth.get(id) ?? 0;
    if (!byDepth.has(d)) byDepth.set(d, []);
    byDepth.get(d)!.push(id);

    const obj = heap[id];
    if (!obj) continue;
    for (const childId of childIdsOf(obj)) {
      if (!depth.has(childId) && heap[childId]) {
        depth.set(childId, d + 1);
        queue.push(childId);
      }
    }
  }

  // Place nodes: x by depth, y by order within the depth column. We vertically
  // center each column so the whole diagram reads as balanced.
  const depths = [...byDepth.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  let maxRows = 0;
  for (const d of depths) maxRows = Math.max(maxRows, byDepth.get(d)!.length);
  const canvasHeight = Math.max(1, maxRows) * ROW_GAP;

  for (const d of depths) {
    const column = byDepth.get(d)!;
    const colHeight = column.length * ROW_GAP;
    const yStart = (canvasHeight - colHeight) / 2;
    column.forEach((id, i) => {
      nodes.set(id, {
        id,
        depth: d,
        x: PAD + d * COL_GAP,
        y: PAD + yStart + i * ROW_GAP,
      });
    });
  }

  const width = PAD * 2 + (depths.length > 0 ? (Math.max(...depths) + 1) * COL_GAP : 0);
  const height = PAD * 2 + canvasHeight;

  return { nodes, width, height };
}

import { useLayoutEffect, useState } from "react";

export interface Connection {
  from: string;
  to: string;
}

export interface ArrowLayerProps {
  /** Container the arrows are drawn over; coordinates are relative to it. */
  containerRef: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
  /** Map of anchor id -> DOM element, populated by the box components. */
  anchors: Map<string, HTMLElement>;
  /** Source -> target connections to draw. */
  connections: Connection[];
  /** Bump this to force a re-measure (e.g. when the step changes). */
  revision: number;
}

type ArrowMode = "horizontal" | "vertical" | "gutter";

interface Segment {
  key: string;
  x1: number;
  y1: number;
  x2: number;
  y2: number;
  mode: ArrowMode;
  /** For gutter arrows: how far left the curve bows (px, container coords). */
  gutterX?: number;
}

function centerRight(r: DOMRect, c: DOMRect) {
  return { x: r.right - c.left, y: r.top - c.top + r.height / 2 };
}
function centerBottom(r: DOMRect, c: DOMRect) {
  return { x: r.left - c.left + r.width / 2, y: r.bottom - c.top };
}
function centerTop(r: DOMRect, c: DOMRect) {
  return { x: r.left - c.left + r.width / 2, y: r.top - c.top };
}
function centerLeft(r: DOMRect, c: DOMRect) {
  return { x: r.left - c.left, y: r.top - c.top + r.height / 2 };
}

/**
 * SVG overlay that draws arrows between anchored boxes. It measures element
 * rects on layout (and on container resize), so arrows follow the boxes.
 * Variable/array-cell -> object arrows leave from the right or bottom of the
 * source and enter the left or top of the target, whichever reads cleaner.
 */
export default function ArrowLayer({
  containerRef,
  anchors,
  connections,
  revision,
}: ArrowLayerProps) {
  const [segments, setSegments] = useState<Segment[]>([]);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const container = containerRef.current;
    if (!container) return;

    const measure = () => {
      const c = container.getBoundingClientRect();
      const next: Segment[] = [];
      for (const conn of connections) {
        const fromEl = anchors.get(conn.from);
        const toEl = anchors.get(conn.to);
        if (!fromEl || !toEl) continue;
        const fr = fromEl.getBoundingClientRect();
        const tr = toEl.getBoundingClientRect();

        const fcx = fr.left + fr.width / 2;
        const tcx = tr.left + tr.width / 2;
        const sameColumn =
          Math.abs(fcx - tcx) < Math.max(fr.width, tr.width) * 1.1;

        let mode: ArrowMode;
        if (sameColumn && Math.abs(tr.top - fr.top) > 6) {
          // Boxes stacked in the same column (e.g. stack variables, or a node
          // above/below). Route the arrow out through the left gutter so it
          // doesn't cut across the boxes between them.
          mode = "gutter";
        } else if (
          tr.top - fr.bottom > -4 &&
          Math.abs(tcx - fcx) < Math.max(fr.width, tr.width) * 2
        ) {
          // Target sits below and roughly aligned: array-of-objects "| V".
          mode = "vertical";
        } else {
          // Default: horizontal, source-right to target-left.
          mode = "horizontal";
        }

        let start: { x: number; y: number };
        let end: { x: number; y: number };
        let gutterX: number | undefined;

        if (mode === "gutter") {
          start = centerRight(fr, c);
          end = centerRight(tr, c);
          // Bow out to the right of whichever box reaches furthest right, into
          // the open space before the heap column.
          const rightMost = Math.max(start.x, end.x);
          gutterX = rightMost + 18;
        } else if (mode === "vertical") {
          start = centerBottom(fr, c);
          end = centerTop(tr, c);
        } else {
          start = centerRight(fr, c);
          end = centerLeft(tr, c);
        }

        next.push({
          key: `${conn.from}->${conn.to}`,
          x1: start.x,
          y1: start.y,
          x2: end.x,
          y2: end.y,
          mode,
          gutterX,
        });
      }
      setSegments(next);
    };

    measure();
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(measure);
    ro.observe(container);
    window.addEventListener("resize", measure);
    return () => {
      ro.disconnect();
      window.removeEventListener("resize", measure);
    };
    // revision forces re-measure when the step/data changes.
  }, [containerRef, anchors, connections, revision]);

  return (
    <svg className="arrow-layer" aria-hidden="true">
      <defs>
        <marker
          id="arrowhead"
          markerWidth="8"
          markerHeight="8"
          refX="6"
          refY="3"
          orient="auto"
        >
          <path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" className="arrow-layer__head" />
        </marker>
      </defs>
      {segments.map((s) => {
        let d: string;
        if (s.mode === "gutter") {
          // Leave the source's left edge, bow out to gutterX, return to the
          // target's left edge. Works for arrows going up or down.
          const gx = s.gutterX ?? Math.min(s.x1, s.x2) - 18;
          const midY = (s.y1 + s.y2) / 2;
          d = `M ${s.x1},${s.y1} C ${gx},${s.y1} ${gx},${midY} ${gx},${midY} C ${gx},${s.y2} ${s.x2},${s.y2} ${s.x2},${s.y2}`;
        } else if (s.mode === "vertical") {
          const midY = (s.y1 + s.y2) / 2;
          d = `M ${s.x1},${s.y1} C ${s.x1},${midY} ${s.x2},${midY} ${s.x2},${s.y2}`;
        } else {
          const midX = (s.x1 + s.x2) / 2;
          d = `M ${s.x1},${s.y1} C ${midX},${s.y1} ${midX},${s.y2} ${s.x2},${s.y2}`;
        }
        return (
          <path
            key={s.key}
            d={d}
            className="arrow-layer__path"
            markerEnd="url(#arrowhead)"
          />
        );
      })}
    </svg>
  );
}

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { ExecutionTrace } from "./trace";

export interface Stepper {
  /** Current step index (clamped to the trace). */
  step: number;
  /** Total number of states. */
  total: number;
  /** True while auto-play is running. */
  playing: boolean;
  /** Delay between auto-play steps, in ms. */
  speedMs: number;

  atStart: boolean;
  atEnd: boolean;

  /** Jump to an arbitrary step (used by the slider). */
  goTo: (step: number) => void;
  /** Step into: advance exactly one execution step (descends into calls). */
  stepInto: () => void;
  /** Step over: run any call on this line to completion, stop at same depth. */
  stepOver: () => void;
  /** Step out: run until we return to a shallower call-stack depth. */
  stepOut: () => void;
  /** Step back one state. */
  stepBack: () => void;
  /** Restart at the first state. */
  restart: () => void;
  /** Toggle auto-play. */
  togglePlay: () => void;
  setSpeedMs: (ms: number) => void;
}

/**
 * Owns playback position over an execution trace and implements the debugger
 * stepping semantics using each state's `depth`:
 *   - step into = next index
 *   - step over = next index whose depth <= current depth
 *   - step out  = next index whose depth <  current depth
 * Depth is optional in the trace; when absent, over/out behave like into.
 */
/**
 * @param trace          the states to scrub through
 * @param jumpToEndOnNew when true, landing on a new trace snaps to its final
 *                       state (used for real run results so the user sees the
 *                       finished program, then steps back). The sample trace
 *                       passes false so it opens at the start.
 */
export function useStepper(
  trace: ExecutionTrace,
  jumpToEndOnNew: boolean = false
): Stepper {
  const states = trace.states;
  const total = states.length;

  const [step, setStep] = useState(0);
  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);
  // Default to 1x (1.5s per state) so learners can follow each change.
  const [speedMs, setSpeedMs] = useState(1500);

  // When a NEW real-run trace arrives, jump to the final state so the user
  // sees the finished result first, then can step BACK through execution to
  // understand how it got there. Detect "new trace" by reference identity.
  const prevTraceRef = useRef<ExecutionTrace | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const changed =
      prevTraceRef.current !== null && prevTraceRef.current !== trace;
    prevTraceRef.current = trace;
    if (changed && jumpToEndOnNew) {
      setPlaying(false);
      setStep(Math.max(0, trace.states.length - 1));
    } else if (changed) {
      // A different (sample) trace: reset to the start.
      setPlaying(false);
      setStep(0);
    }
  }, [trace, jumpToEndOnNew]);

  // Keep step in range if the trace shrinks (e.g. a new run).
  const clamped = Math.min(step, Math.max(0, total - 1));
  const atStart = clamped <= 0;
  const atEnd = clamped >= total - 1;

  const depthAt = useCallback(
    (i: number) => states[i]?.depth ?? 1,
    [states]
  );
